intended_object: The canonical S-linear isomorphism H₁(L_{S/P}) ≅ H₁(L_{S/P}) between the first homology of the naive cotangent complex computed from the presentation P (where P is an extension of S over R, now viewed as an extension of S over its own ring P) and the canonical first homology `Algebra.H1Cotangent P.Ring S`. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition applies `Extension.H1Cotangent.equiv`, Mathlib's canonical isomorphism between the H₁ of the naive cotangent complexes of any two extensions of the same algebra (H₁ does not depend on the presentation). It takes the two extensions `P.extendScalars` and the default extension `Generators.self P.Ring S`. The two homomorphisms between them are `ofAlgHom (Algebra.ofId _ _)` and `defaultHom`. So the map is exactly the canonical isomorphism that the docstring describes.

The setting is fully general: arbitrary commutative rings R and S, and an extension in an arbitrary universe. The definition is not a duplicate of a more general Mathlib construction; it specialises that general equivalence to the extension `P.extendScalars`. It is a canonical map, not an auxiliary device, and the library uses it to build `h1CotangentEquivCotangent`.
